# LLVM InstCombine rewrite inventory

**Work in progress — all source files have been reviewed, but Puddle implementation and proof work is incomplete.** Pending entries are neither unsupported cases nor proved rewrites. Source descriptions remain subject to correction during implementation.

Target: [`29eff20316c550d8e689a318c614e40186107820`](https://github.com/llvm/llvm-project/commit/29eff20316c550d8e689a318c614e40186107820), the `main` tip resolved at 2026-10-18T07:31:28.920038+00:00.

Commit: [TableGen][NFC] Fix stale header path in Target.td comment (#233015) (2026-10-18T07:25:01Z). The local source snapshot is hash checked by `Tools/InstCombine/build_catalog.py` against `llvm-pin.json`.

Scope: transformations defined in `llvm/lib/Transforms/InstCombine/`, including instruction replacement, operand mutation, flags, and metadata changes. Calls into transformations defined elsewhere (for example InstSimplify or libcall simplification) are delegation sites, not an inventory of those external implementations. Helper-generated and visitor rewrites must be reconciled to avoid duplicate counts.

An entry describes a source transformation branch or an explicitly parameterized family; this is not a count of all possible type/constant instantiations. `candidate-sites.json` is a mechanical checklist of return/mutation locations, including non-rewrites. It does not establish exhaustive coverage. Coverage manifests retain unfinished source ranges.

Puddle validity means `Veir.Puddle.Pattern.Valid` under the repository’s interpreter and refinement model. Implementation/proof counts count source entries with at least one recorded pattern in the stated proof scope; they do not assert that every upstream variant is covered. A theorem for a scalar or concrete recursive specialization is not proof of the full LLVM vector or recursive family. LLVM behavior outside that model must be documented separately. No counterexample is evidence of an LLVM bug unless it satisfies the original LLVM guards and semantics.

Current checkpoint: **126 source entries with Puddle implementations**, **123 with currently validated proofs**, **3 counterexamples**, **1088 confirmed unsupported**, and **1016 pending outcomes**. The implementations contain 533 pattern variants, of which 530 have currently validated proofs.

Within implemented entries, **0 lack a recorded source-scope review** and **15 entries record supported variants still pending**. These counts may overlap. A proved specialization does not close its source entry until remaining supported variants and unsupported model cases are accounted for.

## InstCombineAddSub.cpp

### faddcombine-L432a

Expand both fadd/fsub addends by one level, collect up to four weighted symbolic terms, combine equal SSA values, and re-emit only if the result fits the instruction quota (at least one instruction saved).

- Source: [InstCombineAddSub.cpp:432–480](https://github.com/llvm/llvm-project/blob/29eff20316c550d8e689a318c614e40186107820/llvm/lib/Transforms/InstCombine/InstCombineAddSub.cpp#L432-L480), `FAddCombine::simplify`.
- Matched opcodes: `fadd`, `fsub`, `fmul`.
- Replacement opcodes: `fadd`, `fsub`, `fmul`, `fneg`.
- Additional conditions: reassoc and nsz flags; scalar FP type; both inputs can be expanded; instruction quota is 1 or 2
- Uses analysis beyond opcode/constant matching: **no dataflow analysis recorded**; structural/type/property/use-count guards may still apply.
- Result: **unsupported**.
- Puddle limitation (confirmed): This is an FP rewrite; Puddle does not represent poisoned floating values and supplies no fast-math/NaN/infinity/signed-zero reasoning required to validate the LLVM branch.

- Result: **pending**.

- Lean: [Veir/Passes/InstCombineLLVM/SubNegRight.lean](../../Veir/Passes/InstCombineLLVM/SubNegRight.lean); theorem `Veir.Passes.InstCombineLLVM.SubNegRight.subNegRight_valid`.

- Additional pattern: [Veir/Passes/InstCombineLLVM/SubNegRight.lean](../../Veir/Passes/InstCombineLLVM/SubNegRight.lean); theorem `Veir.Passes.InstCombineLLVM.SubNegRight.subNegConstant_valid`. Arbitrary-width scalar IntegerAttr arm of dyn_castNegVal; matches any normalized literal, creates its typed modular negation, and clears result flags.
- Additional pattern: [Veir/Passes/InstCombineLLVM/SubNegRight.lean](../../Veir/Passes/InstCombineLLVM/SubNegRight.lean); theorem `Veir.Passes.InstCombineLLVM.SubNegRight.subNegConstantNSW_valid`. Arbitrary-width scalar NSW-preserving IntegerAttr arm when the root subtraction is NSW and the matched literal is not the signed minimum; NUW remains unrestricted and is cleared.
- Proof scope: Scalar integers of arbitrary width for X-(-A) -> X+A. Explicit subtraction negations and scalar IntegerAttr negations are covered. Conservative variants accept arbitrary source nsw/nuw flags and clear result flags. NSW variants preserve nsw under the source guards: both subtractions are nsw for an explicit negation, or the root is nsw and the literal is not signed-min for an IntegerAttr negation. Poison and overflow-to-poison are modeled; created constants retain the matched type and use modular normalization.
- Full source-scope review: complete.

### bitwise-L5187

For `z = ~(x &/| y)`, rewrite the logical operation to the De Morgan equivalent by inverting both operands, replacing the root with the opposite logical operator, and recursively inverting all users. At a scalar root this has the direct equivalent `not(and(x,y)) = or(not x,not y)` or `not(or(x,y)) = and(not x,not y)`; source implements the full use-graph update.

- Source: [InstCombineAndOrXor.cpp:5163–5192](https://github.com/llvm/llvm-project/blob/29eff20316c550d8e689a318c614e40186107820/llvm/lib/Transforms/InstCombine/InstCombineAndOrXor.cpp#L5163-L5192), `InstCombinerImpl::sinkNotIntoLogicalOp`.
- Matched opcodes: `and`, `or`, `select`, `xor`.
- Replacement opcodes: `and`, `or`, `select`, `xor`.
- Additional conditions: source logical operation is AND or OR (binary or logical/select form); operands are distinct and neither is the NOT of the other; all required operand/root users are freely invertible and valid insertion points exist; source swaps select profile metadata when rebuilding logical/select form; direct scalar root De Morgan equivalent is expressible; the full source algorithm additionally mutates non-root users
- Uses analysis beyond opcode/constant matching: **yes**.
- Result: **pending**.
- Puddle limitation (requires verification): The exact scalar root De Morgan expression is representable. The complete LLVM algorithm requires recursively updating operand/root users and insertion points, which Puddle cannot express as a single root replacement.

### atomicrmw-L112

For non-volatile atomicrmw with a saturating value, mutate the operation to xchg while retaining the operand. Exact integer cases: xchg; or all-ones; and zero; signed min with signed minimum; signed max with signed maximum; unsigned min with unsigned minimum; unsigned max with unsigned maximum. Exact FP cases: fmax +infinity; fmin -infinity; fadd/fsub NaN.

- Source: [InstCombineAtomicRMW.cpp:110–116](https://github.com/llvm/llvm-project/blob/29eff20316c550d8e689a318c614e40186107820/llvm/lib/Transforms/InstCombine/InstCombineAtomicRMW.cpp#L110-L116), `InstCombinerImpl::visitAtomicRMWInst`.

- Proof scope: All modeled scalar eliminable cast pairs in the LLVM table are covered. IntegerType rows use arbitrary valid widths, including trunc/trunc, zext/zext, sext/sext, zext/sext, every extension followed by trunc width ordering, and the integer bitcast rows. The seven additional same-width IntegerType/ByteType triples are covered at arbitrary nonzero widths; B->I->B uses refinement because whole-value integer poison may discard per-bit information. The memory-independent pointer subset covers same-address-space P->P->P, P->P->B, P->B->B, and P->B->I (the last emits ptrtoint), with byte/integer pointer endpoints fixed by the modeled 64-bit pointer width. All source poison flags are modeled and replacement flags are cleared exactly where LLVM creates an unflagged cast.
- Full source-scope review: complete.
- Source variants blocked by the model: vector and scalar/vector bitcast forms lack elementwise vector cast semantics; floating cast pairs lack complete poison/FP semantics; pointer cast-pair cases that construct a pointer from integer or byte bits remain unsupported: Puddle inttoptr/byte-to-pointer reconstruction depends on MemoryState under the all-memory InterpretsTo contract
- Validation: lake build Veir.Passes.InstCombineLLVM.ComposeZExt Veir.Passes.InstCombineLLVM.ComposeBitcastScalar UnitTest.InstCombineLLVMCastsIntrinsics; Tools/InstCombine/check_proofs.py

The source helper may recursively simplify the wide negation and applies its own use/depth profitability checks, which this local semantic pattern does not model.

The registered arbitrary-width commute pattern proves the local semantic law by materializing the wide negation, and the double-negation pattern records one exact recursive specialization.

### select-L2629-fp

- Uses analysis beyond opcode/constant matching: **no dataflow analysis recorded**; structural/type/property/use-count guards may still apply.

### shift-L176

For outer shl of a recognized mask/shift-mask on X, replace the masked value with X shifted by S, optionally retaining an output mask. Exact matched forms are: (X & ((1<<M)-1))<<S; (X & ~(-1<<M))<<S; (X & (-1 lshr M))<<S; (X & ((-1<<M) lshr M))<<S; ((X<<M) lshr M)<<S; and ((X<<M) ashr M)<<S. The first two derive a low-bit output mask from M+S; the latter four derive a high-bit output mask from S-M. In each case emit shl(X,S) directly when the derived mask is all ones, otherwise emit and(shl(X,S),mask), truncating X first if the matched inner expression crossed a trunc.

- Source: [InstCombineShifts.cpp:193–351](https://github.com/llvm/llvm-project/blob/29eff20316c550d8e689a318c614e40186107820/llvm/lib/Transforms/InstCombine/InstCombineShifts.cpp#L193-L351), `dropRedundantMaskingOfLeftShiftInput`.

- Replacement opcodes: `shl`, `and`, `trunc`.
- Additional conditions: input opcode is shl; one of the six exact mask/shift-back forms above matches (including source-level optional zext of M or S); canTryToConstantAddTwoShiftAmounts proves amount addition cannot overflow; low-mask cases require simplified M+S; high-mask/shift-back cases require simplified S-M; type can be doubled for mask computation; if a trunc separates outer shift and mask, trunc is one-use; if output mask is nontrivial, masked input is one-use and cannot be ashr; no nowrap flags are retained; amount sums/differences must simplify to constants; these are fixed-width constant-folding conditions, not KnownBits analysis
- Uses analysis beyond opcode/constant matching: **no dataflow analysis recorded**; structural/type/property/use-count guards may still apply.
- Result: **pending**.

### ic-inttoptr-ptrtoint-roundtrip-L434

Replace inttoptr(ptrtoint(p)) with p when pointer and integer widths agree at both casts and both pointer address spaces match.

- Source: [InstructionCombining.cpp:434–451](https://github.com/llvm/llvm-project/blob/29eff20316c550d8e689a318c614e40186107820/llvm/lib/Transforms/InstCombine/InstructionCombining.cpp#L434-L451), `simplifyIntToPtrRoundTripCast`.

- Uses analysis beyond opcode/constant matching: **yes**.
- Result: **unsupported**.
- Additional replacement details: `pointer`.
- Puddle limitation (confirmed): The meaningful pointer roundtrip requires memory-state-aware provenance semantics: inttoptr reconstructs object identity via MemoryState.ptrFromInt/decode, while InterpretsTo requires one fixed result for every memory state. The resulting nonpoison premise can be vacuous; scalar i64 opcode support alone cannot establish this source identity. Other pointer widths/address spaces also lack modeled cast semantics. See puddle-capabilities.md pointer discussion.
- Reason: Puddle InterpretsTo requires one fixed result for every memory state, but inttoptr reconstructs pointer object identity through memory-dependent ptrFromInt/decode. It therefore cannot faithfully express the nonpoison source cast's behavior across arbitrary memories; proving the rule from an impossible fixed-result premise would be vacuous. Pointer/object consistency across a memory and a supplied SSA pointer is also absent from the pattern premises. A state-aware pointer semantics is needed, in addition to the full LLVM width/address-space conditions.
- Proof scope: The general equal-width same-address-space inttoptr(ptrtoint(P)) -> P branch, including its 64-bit nonpoison specialization.
- Validation: Inspected pinned InstructionCombining.cpp:434-445; Veir/PatternRewriter/Puddle/Validity.lean:511-514; Veir/Dialects/LLVM/OpInfo.lean:1656-1665; Veir/Interpreter/Memory.lean:95-110,180-182. This is a proof-model limitation, not an LLVM counterexample.

### ic-visit-gep-normalize-indices-L3346

Canonicalize each non-struct GEP index to the DataLayout index width: sign-extend narrow indices (or zext nneg when GEP has both nuw and nusw), truncate wide indices with compatible flags, and replace displacement through a zero-size element by a typed zero index.

- Source: [InstructionCombining.cpp:3375–3421](https://github.com/llvm/llvm-project/blob/29eff20316c550d8e689a318c614e40186107820/llvm/lib/Transforms/InstCombine/InstructionCombining.cpp#L3375-L3421), `visitGetElementPtrInst`.
- Matched opcodes: `getelementptr`.
- Replacement opcodes: `getelementptr`, `sext`, `zext`, `trunc`.
- Additional conditions: Skip struct indices; choose scalar or corresponding vector DataLayout index type.; Replace a nonzero/nonconstant index over a sized zero-allocation-size element by typed zero.; For differing index widths, narrow-to-wide uses sext unless both GEP nuw and nusw permit zext nneg; wide-to-narrow trunc receives the corresponding nuw/nsw flags.; Return the mutated GEP if any index changed; earlier external simplification and demanded-vector dispatches are separate delegation entries.
- Uses analysis beyond opcode/constant matching: **yes**.
- Result: **counterexample**.
- Audit note: The original umbrella span included external simplifyGEPInst and demanded-vector dispatch. Those now have separate delegation entries; the local index normalization family starts at the non-struct index loop setup. Extension/truncation opcodes are created outputs, not required matched producer opcodes.
- Lean: [Veir/Passes/InstCombineLLVM/GEPIndexNormalizationCounterexample.lean](../../Veir/Passes/InstCombineLLVM/GEPIndexNormalizationCounterexample.lean); theorem `Veir.Passes.InstCombineLLVM.GEPIndexNormalizationCounterexample.normalizeNarrowGepIndex_not_valid`.
- Reason: Puddle's llvm.getelementptr interpreter converts every dynamic integer index with BitVec.toNat, independent of its original width. LLVM interprets a narrow GEP index as sign-extended to the target index width, so making that sign extension explicit must preserve LLVM behavior but changes Puddle behavior for a negative narrow index. This is a Puddle model counterexample, not evidence of an LLVM bug.
- Proof scope: RV64 scalar specialization with a free pointer base, a free i8 dynamic index, i8 element stride, and no GEP nowrap flags. The source GEP and replacement GEP after sext i8 to i64 are modeled by the executable pattern. At index 255 and base address zero, Puddle evaluates the source with unsigned BitVec.toNat to address 255 but evaluates the sign-extended replacement to address 2^64-1.
- Full source-scope review: complete.
- Supported variants still to implement/prove: other narrow-to-i64 scalar index widths, including the nuw+nusw zext nneg arm; wide scalar index truncation to the RV64 index width with propagated nowrap flags; replacement of indices over sized zero-allocation-size elements by a typed zero
- Source variants blocked by the model: vector GEP indices lack modeled elementwise vector cast and GEP semantics; struct-index traversal and multi-index GEPs are not supported by Puddle's one-dynamic-index GEP interpreter
- Validation: lake build Veir.Passes.InstCombineLLVM.GEPIndexNormalizationCounterexample UnitTest.InstCombineLLVMGEPCounterexample; Tools/InstCombine/check_proofs.py

### ic-freeze-push-through-op-L5236

Push freeze through a one-use non-PHI operation that cannot create poison except by flags, dropping such flags and freezing its unique operand not proven nonpoison; if all operands nonpoison, remove freeze.

- Source: [InstructionCombining.cpp:5236–5296](https://github.com/llvm/llvm-project/blob/29eff20316c550d8e689a318c614e40186107820/llvm/lib/Transforms/InstCombine/InstructionCombining.cpp#L5236-L5296), `pushFreezeToPreventPoisonFromPropagating`.

- Additional conditions: operand one-use; op cannot create poison except annotations; at most one operand not guaranteed nonpoison; GuaranteedNotToBeUndefOrPoison analysis; scoped proof candidate: scalar integer add without poison-generating flags, one operand a nonpoison constant, freeze the other operand; do not rely on source analysis facts
- Uses analysis beyond opcode/constant matching: **yes**.
- Result: **counterexample**.
- Additional match details: `cast`.
- Additional replacement details: `cast`.
- Audit note: The scalar counterexample is implemented, executes with source eligibility guards, and has an independently checked theorem of type not Pattern.Valid. LLVM.Int.freeze explicitly chooses zero for poison (Veir/Data/LLVM/Int/Basic.lean:845-852); see the registered negative proof and verified-counterexamples.json.
- Puddle limitation (confirmed): The interpreter fixes freeze(poison) to zero. A formal not-Valid proof establishes that the eligible scalar specialization freeze(add X,1) -> add(freeze X,1) gives 0 versus 1 for poison X. This is a limitation of deterministic freeze semantics, not an LLVM bug. Full source scope additionally includes dataflow and non-root mutation requirements.
- Lean: [Veir/Passes/InstCombineLLVM/FreezePushThroughAddCounterexample.lean](../../Veir/Passes/InstCombineLLVM/FreezePushThroughAddCounterexample.lean); theorem `Veir.Passes.InstCombineLLVM.FreezePushThroughAddCounterexample.freezePushThroughAdd_not_valid`.
- Reason: Puddle models `freeze poison` as deterministic zero. This makes pushing freeze through addition observably change the modeled result for poison X and constant 1. This is a Puddle model counterexample, not evidence of an LLVM bug because LLVM freeze may choose an arbitrary value.
- Proof scope: Width-2 scalar unflagged add specialization `freeze (X + 1) -> freeze X + 1`; the constant is nonpoison and the add has one use, so the modeled fixture satisfies the source eligibility guards. With X poison, Puddle deterministically evaluates the source to 0 and the target to 1.
- Full source-scope review: complete.
- Source variants blocked by the model: The counterexample is intentionally scalar; Puddle integer runtime values do not model LLVM vectors.; The full upstream routine mutates non-root operations and uses poison dataflow analysis; this executable Puddle pattern models the eligible one-use add specialization directly.
- Validation: lake build Veir.Passes.InstCombineLLVM.FreezePushThroughAddCounterexample UnitTest.InstCombineLLVMModelCounterexamples; Tools/InstCombine/check_proofs.py

- Result: **counterexample**.

- Audit note: The scalar poison alternative is modeled and requires proof/counterexample work. Actual undef and aggregate forms remain outside the interpreter; the full multi-user choice also requires use-graph/analysis support. Deterministic freeze may refute the scalar all-ones choice; no counterexample is counted until its negative theorem passes validation.
- Lean: [Veir/Passes/InstCombineLLVM/FreezeUndefUseChoiceCounterexample.lean](../../Veir/Passes/InstCombineLLVM/FreezeUndefUseChoiceCounterexample.lean); theorem `Veir.Passes.InstCombineLLVM.FreezeUndefUseChoiceCounterexample.freezePoisonOrAllOnes_not_valid`.
- Reason: LLVM's `m_Undef` matcher also accepts poison, and the OR-only user choice replaces `freeze poison` with all ones. Puddle instead models `freeze poison` as deterministic zero, so this eligible scalar specialization changes the modeled result. This is a Puddle model counterexample, not evidence of an LLVM bug because LLVM freeze may choose the all-ones value consistently.
- Proof scope: Width-2 scalar one-use OR specialization of the use-based replacement: `or (freeze poison), Y -> or -1, Y`, preserving the source OR properties. The runtime fixture establishes that the freeze has exactly one OR use. With Y=0, Puddle evaluates the source to 0 and the target to all ones.
- Full source-scope review: complete.
- Source variants blocked by the model: The counterexample is intentionally scalar; Puddle integer runtime values do not model LLVM vectors or the shuffle-use exclusion.; The full upstream routine chooses one value across every freeze use, including select and PHI users. This executable Puddle pattern models the concrete one-use OR specialization, where replacing the root context is equivalent to replacing the freeze's sole use.; Puddle has no distinct undef runtime value; the formal witness uses the poison alternative accepted by LLVM's `m_Undef` matcher.
- Validation: lake build Veir.Passes.InstCombineLLVM.FreezeUndefUseChoiceCounterexample UnitTest.InstCombineLLVMModelCounterexamples; Tools/InstCombine/check_proofs.py
